title: 6.036 Introduction to Machine Learning, Fall 2020 - Tamara Broderick
description: In Fall 2020 I gave the lectures for MIT's 6.036 course: Introduction to Machine Learning. Below is a set of links to those lectures. Each link will be provided once captioning is completed for the corresponding video. A playlist of all the videos available so far can be found at the following link: . Note: I will try to release errata and slides with corrections relative to the live lectures here, as necessary. * Lecture 1: Basics (2020 / 09 / 01). * Lecture 2: Perceptrons (2020 / 09 / 08). * Lecture 6: Neural networks (2020 / 10 / 06). * Lecture 7: There was a holiday this week, and the lecture numbering matches the week of the course. * Lecture 8: Convolutional neural networks (2020 / 10 / 20). * Lecture 10: Reinforcement learning (2020 / 11 / 03). * Lecture 11: Recurrent neural networks (2020 / 11 / 10). * The 6.036 Fall 2020 course staff (instructors, TAs, and LAs) and past 6.036 course staff.

title: Notes – Chapters 1 and 2 | Introduction to ML | 6.036 Courseware | MIT Open Learning Library
description: The main focus of machine learning is *making decisions or predictions based on data*. There are a number of other fields with significant overlap in technique, but This story paraphrased from a post on 9/4/12 at andrewgelman.comdifference in focus:  in economics and psychology, the goal is to discover underlying causal processes and in statistics it is to find a model that fits a data set well. In machine learning, we often fit models, but as a means to the end of making good predictions or decisions. We will operationalize it by making assumptions, such as that all training data are IID (independent and identically distributed) and that queries will be drawn from the same distribution as the training data, or that the answer comes from a set of possible answers known in advance.
